The unique solution is:

| Day | Person | Pet |
|---|---|---|
| Monday | Cho | fish |
| Tuesday | Ada | hen |
| Wednesday | Ben | dog |
| Thursday | Dia | cat |
| Friday | Eno | owl |

**Why this is the only solution:**

- Dia works exactly two days after the hen owner, so the possible hen/Dia day pairs are:  
  Monday/Wednesday, Tuesday/Thursday, or Wednesday/Friday.
- If the hen owner were Monday, Dia would be Wednesday, forcing Ben to be Thursday. But then the fish owner cannot be Monday, and putting the fish on Tuesday leaves no room for both Ada and Eno after it. Impossible.
- If the hen owner were Wednesday, Dia would be Friday. Whether Ben is Wednesday or Thursday, the only way to satisfy “fish earlier than Ada earlier than Eno” forces the fish on Monday and Ada on Tuesday, with the cat and dog ending up on non-adjacent days. That violates the dog/cat adjacency rule. Impossible.
- Therefore the hen owner must be Tuesday and Dia must be Thursday. Then Ben must be Wednesday.

With Dia on Thursday and Ben on Wednesday, the remaining people Ada, Cho, and Eno must take Monday, Tuesday, and Friday. Since the fish owner is earlier than Ada, and Ada is earlier than Eno, and Tuesday is the hen owner, the only possibility is:

- Fish owner: Monday → Cho
- Ada: Tuesday → hen
- Eno: Friday

The owl must be Monday or Friday; Monday is already fish, so Friday’s Eno owns the owl. The remaining pets for Ben and Dia are dog and cat on adjacent days Wednesday/Thursday. Since Dia does not own the dog, Dia owns the cat and Ben owns the dog.
